title: Start a new chat for each task
body: Old turns are re-sent and billed with every prompt, and they pull answers off topic.

title: Glance at the context window control
body: Hover it to see tokens and credits used. Act at about half full, not when it’s already squeezing.

title: Compact with a focus
body: “/compact keep the API decisions” keeps what you need. Automatic compaction guesses.

title: Leave the model on Auto for routine work
body: Auto saves costly reasoning models for hard problems and gets a small discount on paid plans.

title: Reference, don’t paste
body: #problems, #terminalSelection and # files add exactly what’s needed. Pasted walls of text add everything.

title: Use inline chat for small, local edits
body: ⌘I / Ctrl+I works on the selection with a tiny context, so it is fast and cheap.

title: Say the goal, the limits and “done when”
body: Copilot can’t read your mind. Clear acceptance criteria stop extra rounds.

title: Plan before multi-file changes
body: Correcting a plan is a few lines. Correcting a wrong implementation is a whole agent run.

title: Put team conventions in instruction files
body: Write them once in .github/copilot-instructions.md instead of repeating them in every prompt. Keep the file short.

title: Save prompts you repeat as prompt files
body: A .prompt.md file runs with /name, so the whole team gets the same tested prompt.

title: Ask for short replies
body: “Reply in 5 lines” cuts output tokens now and history tokens on every later prompt.

title: Read every diff before keeping it
body: You own the code, not Copilot. Review it like a colleague’s pull request.

title: Make Copilot prove it works
body: Ask it to run the tests or build and show the result. “Looks right” isn’t evidence.

title: Commit small and often
body: A bad change is cheap to undo when the last good state is one commit away.

title: Keep tool approvals on
body: Default (manual) permissions let you see each command before it runs. Approve for the session, not forever.

title: Follow your company AI policy
body: It decides which repos, data and models are allowed. This guide doesn’t override it.

title: Run one chat all day
body: Every prompt drags the whole day’s history along, and you pay for it each time.

title: Paste whole logs or files
body: A 2,000-line log can fill a large part of the window for one line of signal.

title: Reach for #codebase when you know the file
body: A project-wide search pulls in lots of code. Attach the file directly.

title: Default to the biggest model
body: Large reasoning models cost more per token and are slower. Most edits don’t need them.

title: Let an agent loop on a failing approach
body: Every retry, file read and test run is billed. Stop it, rethink, and restart with a better prompt.

title: Keep correcting in a muddled thread
body: Two wrong answers? The bad attempts are now part of the context. /clear and restate the problem properly.

title: Write “fix it” or “make it better”
body: Vague prompts get vague code and extra rounds. Name the file, the symptom and the expected result.

title: Retype the same conventions every time
body: Put them in an instructions file once. Then keep that file short, because it’s sent on every request.

title: Keep code you don’t understand
body: If you can’t explain it in review, you can’t support it in production.

title: Trust package names and APIs blindly
body: Models can invent functions, options and even packages. Check the docs or the type definitions.

title: Let Copilot commit or push unreviewed
body: An agent that can run git can push mistakes. Review, then commit yourself.

title: Paste secrets, tokens or customer data
body: Prompts leave your machine. Use placeholders and fake data.

title: Turn on global auto-approve
body: chat.tools.global.autoApprove approves every tool; VS Code warns that it disables critical security protections.

title: Assume content exclusion covers Agent mode
body: Content exclusion isn’t supported in Edit and Agent modes. Excluded files can still be read by the agent.
